title: Control Plane weekwrap + open issues (Jan 5 2027)
content:
Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Priya, Liam, Ruth, (async notes from Aaron and Sofia)

Purpose: quick weekwrap for the control plane pod — capture 2 things we shipped, 2 ongoing risks, 3 action items for next week, and a short incident retrospective from Wed 2027-01-04. Keep terse; this is what we read before next standup.

1) Highlights shipped this week
- Routing: deployed dynamic-route-scaling v2 to canary (10% traffic) — initial results: 13% decrease in hot-shard queuing for model groups with >300 active prefixes. Canary metrics posted in the dashboard (link above).
- Quotas: prototype soft-limit notifications added to the quota service so product teams receive warnings at 70/85/95% commit utilization instead of only hard rejections. Configurable via per-tenant policy.

2) Incident mini-retro (2027-01-04, ~11:32–12:04 UTC)
- Symptom: short spike of 5xx errors for hosted customers during a cross-region routing change.
- Root cause: controlplane routing cache invalidation logic sent stale route tombstones; downstream allocator briefly returned empty allocations for a small set of tenant-model combos. This was triggered by a simultaneous rollback + rollout from the release pipeline.
- Impact: ~0.4% of requests for the hour, predominantly during the rollback window; no data loss.
- What we learned: cache invalidation must be transactional with the rollout state machine. Current invariant assumptions weren't enforced during fast rollbacks.
- Immediate fix applied: stop-gap: rollback of the rollout service changes (PR 542) and re-enable a short-lived holding-back TTL on tombstones (config override).
- Follow-ups: scoped reliability ticket (JIRA-6324) assigned to Ethan to design transactional invalidation; ETA for spec 2027-01-11.

3) Ongoing risks & signals to watch
- Auth token surge risk: we saw a 2x increase in token validation calls from a pilot customer using frequent ephemeral keys. If this pattern grows, token validation CPU will spike on the auth proxies. Priya to propose caching or a per-key rate limiter.
- Quota enforcement race: when cache misses occur during quota lookups, we have a small window where double-counts can happen. Observed under high concurrency in canary. Proposal: adopt an atomic increment path in the quota store or use optimistic dedupe tokens.
- Cross-region rollout coupling: the deployment coordination logic still has some edge cases when rollouts and force-rollbacks overlap. This ties back to the incident above.

4) Action items (owners + rough ETA)
- Ethan: draft spec for transactional routing-cache invalidation + rollout state machine changes (JIRA-6324). Due 2027-01-11.
- Priya: implement short-term auth token caching (local LRU) on proxy for pilot customer and add telemetry to measure hit-rate; PR targeted 2027-01-10.
- Liam: quota store PoC for atomic increment using Redis lua fallback (or Postgres advisory locks) — spike to evaluate latency impact. Spike ends 2027-01-07; decision by 2027-01-12.
- Ruth: update runbook for routing rollback -> ensure feature flag gate + automated rollback cooldown (update runbook page and attach example CLI commands). Finish by 2027-01-08.

5) Design notes / proposals for discussion in next deep-dive (Thu 1/7)
- Proposal A (Ethan): Use a two-phase commit between rollout-controller and routing-cache: prepare tombstones + mark rollout state, then commit tombstones. This reduces windows where tombstones are visible without rollout state. Pros: simpler invariants; Cons: increases coordination latency.
- Proposal B (Liam): Move quota enforcement into the serving runtime cheaply for high-throughput tenants (use local counters + async durable accounting). Pros: reduces control plane pressure; Cons: increases complexity at runtime and eventual consistency concerns.

6) Quick numbers snapshot (from dashboards, baseline = previous week)
- Control plane p95 API latency: 245ms -> 260ms (up; partly due to canary workload).
- Error rate (5xx) control plane: 0.06% -> 0.32% (bump from incident window).
- Auth proxy CPU: 42% -> 58% for the pilot tenant traffic spike.
- Quota service eviction rate: +12% on cache misses for canary traffic.

7) TODOs / smaller housekeeping items
- Maya: file short RFC for rollout cooldown param default change and include migration notes for Dedicated customers.
- Team: tag affected product teams about the soft-limit notification behavior (customer-facing wording needed). Priya to draft copy.
- Ops: increase monitoring retention for routing cache diffs to 14 days so we can correlate tombstone churn; request sent to observability (ticket JIRA-6389).

8) Open questions we want input on from SRE and Runtime teams
- How much extra latency can we afford in the rollout path for a two-phase commit? (SLO budget check)
- If we move quota enforcement to runtime for select tenants, what security/tenant-isolation concerns come up? (runtime team)
- Do we want to add a short-lived global circuit-breaker for token validation to protect proxies from bursty key churn? If yes, what should the default thresholds be? (SRE + Security)

9) Notes to self / rough ideas
- Consider a TTL-based tombstone staging area: tombstones are staged for Xs, visible only to rollout-controller until commit. Might be easier than full 2PC.
- Could we leverage the allocator's existing lease mechanism to reject allocations when rollout state != committed? Fewer moving parts if allocator enforces consistency.

Appendix: Relevant links and context (copy of links in header)
- Incident ticket: JIRA-6324
- Quota race spike: JIRA-6389
- PR for rollback changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/542
- Slack thread with initial triage: https://slack-redwood.slack.com/archives/C01PLTFM/p1672500000000

If anything is missing or you want to split the spec work across 2 people, call it out in comments here. Otherwise we'll go with owners above and review progress in Thu deep-dive.

-- Maya
